<system-reminder>
## Swarm Mode

You are now in "agent swarm" mode. The user may send tasks that require a large number of parallel subagents.

## Workflow

You do not need to use TodoList to record this workflow.

1. First, you may need to do a small amount of exploratory work before deciding how to divide the task across subagents. You may not need subagents during this exploratory phase.

2. After exploring, if you are convinced no subagent is needed to complete the task, tell the user why and wait for further instructions; otherwise, continue with the appropriate delegation.

3. Once you have enough context, do not handle the main work yourself. Use AgentSwarm with a `prompt_template` containing the `{{item}}` placeholder and an `items` array for the requested or appropriate number of subagents, partitioning the problem so each item gives one subagent a distinct part of the work. Pass `subagent_type` when the whole swarm should use a non-default subagent profile.

## Coordination

- Give each subagent a distinct scope of work.
- Avoid duplicating work across subagents.
- Avoid assigning conflicting changes or responsibilities to different subagents.
- Remember that subagents have your full capabilities. Do not overload their prompts with excessive detail; only describe the necessary background and each subagent's specific task.
- Unless the user explicitly specifies a lower limit, do not try to conserve the number of agents. AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents and queues launches automatically, so decompose work as finely as possible while keeping subagent responsibilities non-conflicting; combine tasks only when they are genuinely inseparable. If the subagents only need to read, inspect, or report back without making changes, their scopes may overlap slightly.
</system-reminder>

payload.prompt:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this - finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool - does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only - your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

title: Cppcheck manual
subtitle: User Guide
author: Cppcheck team
lang: en
documentclass: report
---

# Introduction

Cppcheck is an analysis tool for C/C++ code. It provides unique code analysis to detect bugs and focuses on detecting undefined behaviour and dangerous coding constructs. The goal is to detect only real errors in the code, and generate as few false positives (wrongly reported warnings) as possible. Cppcheck is designed to analyze your C/C++ code even if it has non-standard syntax, as is common in for example embedded projects.

Supported code and platforms:

- Cppcheck checks non-standard code that contains various compiler extensions, inline assembly code, etc.
- Cppcheck is cross platform and is used in various posix/windows/etc environments.

The checks in Cppcheck are not perfect. There are bugs that should be found, that Cppcheck fails to detect.

## About static analysis

The kinds of bugs that you can find with static analysis are:

- Undefined behavior
- Using dangerous code patterns
- Coding style

There are many bugs that you can not find with static analysis. Static analysis tools do not have human knowledge about what your program is intended to do. If the output from your program is valid but unexpected then in most cases this is not detected by static analysis tools. For instance, if your small program writes "Helo" on the screen instead of "Hello" it is unlikely that any tool will complain about that.

Static analysis should be used as a complement in your quality assurance. It does not replace any of:

- Careful design
- Testing
- Dynamic analysis
- Fuzzing

# Getting started

## GUI

It is not required but creating a new project file is a good first step. There are a few options you can tweak to get good results.

In the project settings dialog, the first option you see is "Import project". It is recommended that you use this feature if you can. Cppcheck can import:

- Visual studio solution / project
- Compile database, which can be generated from CMake/qbs/etc build files
- Borland C++ Builder 6

When you have filled out the project settings and clicked on OK, the Cppcheck analysis will start.

## Command line

### First test

Here is some simple code:

    int main()
    {
        char a[10];
        a[10] = 0;
        return 0;
    }

If you save that into file1.c and execute:

    cppcheck file1.c

The output from Cppcheck will then be:

    Checking file1.c...
    [file1.c:4]: (error) Array 'a[10]' index 10 out of bounds

### Checking all files in a folder

Normally a program has many source files. Cppcheck can check all source files in a directory:

    cppcheck path

If "path" is a folder, then Cppcheck will recursively check all source files in this folder:

Cppcheck - A tool for static C/C++ code analysis

Syntax:
    cppcheck [OPTIONS] [files or paths]

If a directory is given instead of a filename, *.cpp, *.cxx, *.cc, *.c++, *.c, *.ipp,

Options:
    --addon=<addon>

                         provided a json configuration is needed.

                         addon json files or through this command line option.
                         If not present, Cppcheck will try "python3" first and
                         then "python".
    --cppcheck-build-dir=<dir>

                          * whole program analysis
                          * faster analysis; Cppcheck will reuse the results if
                            the hash for a file is unchanged.
                          * some useful debug information, i.e. commands used to
                            execute clang/clang-tidy/addons.
    --check-config       Check cppcheck configuration. The normal code
                         analysis is disabled by this flag.
    --check-level=<level>
                         Configure how much valueflow analysis you want:
                          * reduced: Reduce valueflow to finish checking quickly.
                          * normal: Cppcheck uses some compromises in the analysis so
                            the checking will finish in reasonable time.
                          * exhaustive: deeper analysis that you choose when you can
                            wait.
                         The default choice is 'normal'.
    --check-library      Show information messages when library files have
                         incomplete info.
    --checkers-report=<file>
                         Write a report of all the active checkers to the given file.
    --clang=<path>       Experimental: Use Clang parser instead of the builtin Cppcheck
                         parser. Takes the executable as optional parameter and
                         defaults to `clang`. Cppcheck will run the given Clang
                         executable, import the Clang AST and convert it into
                         Cppcheck data. After that the normal Cppcheck analysis is
                         used. You must have the executable in PATH if no path is
                         given.
    --config-exclude=<dir>
                         Path (prefix) to be excluded from configuration
                         checking. Preprocessor configurations defined in
                         headers (but not sources) matching the prefix will not
                         be considered for evaluation.
    --config-excludes-file=<file>
                         A file that contains a list of config-excludes
    --disable=<severity> Disable checks with the given severity.
                         Please refer to the documentation of --enable for
                         further details.
    --dump               Dump xml data for each translation unit. The dump
                         files have the extension .dump and contain ast,
                         tokenlist, symboldatabase, valueflow.
    -D<ID>               Define preprocessor symbol. Unless --max-configs or
                         --force is used, Cppcheck will only check the given
                         configuration when -D is used.
                         Example: '-DDEBUG=1 -D__cplusplus'.
    -E                   Print preprocessor output on stdout and don't do any
                         further processing.
    --enable=<severity>  Enable additional checks grouped by severity. The available

                          * warning

                                  'performance' and 'portability'.

                                  to only enable this when the whole program is
                                  scanned.
                          * missingInclude
                                  Check for missing include files.
                          * all
                                  Enable all checks.
                         Pass multiple severities as a comma-separated list.
    --error-exitcode=<n> If errors are found, integer [n] is returned instead of
                         the default '0'. '1' is returned
                         if arguments are not valid or if no input files are
                         provided. Note that your operating system can modify
                         this value, e.g. '256' can become '0'.
    --errorlist          Print a list of all the error messages in XML format.
    --exitcode-suppressions=<file>
                         Used when certain messages should be displayed but
                         should not cause a non-zero exitcode.

                         filter will be read from standard input. When str is '+',
                         given files on CLI will be treated as file filters.
                         Example: --file-filter=*bar.cpp analyzes only files
                         that end with bar.cpp.

Probe options that reference external files/dirs, recording exact stdout/stderr/exit for each, always also with a.c as the analysis target: --project=nosuch.sln, --project=nosuch.vcxproj, --project=nosuch.bpr, --project=nosuch.json (compile_commands.json), --project with a malformed compile_commands.json file you create, and with a VALID `[]` compile_commands.json; --library=nosuch; --library=std (does it find std?); --rule-file=nosuch, --rule-file with a malformed XML file, --rule-file with a minimal valid rule file; --rule='a.*b' valid regex, --rule='[' invalid regex; --suppressions-list=nosuch, and with a file containing a bogus suppression line; --suppress-xml=nosuch, malformed XML; --exitcode-suppressions=nosuch; --includes-file=nosuch, --includes-file with a file of paths; --file-list=nosuch, --file-list with a file listing a.c and a nonexistent file, --file-list=- with stdin; --config-excludes-file=nosuch; --addon=nosuch, --addon=misra, --addon=/tmp/x.py; --cppcheck-build-dir=/tmp/probe_fileopts/build (does it create the dir before failing? what files appear?); --output-file=/tmp/probe_fileopts/out.txt a.c — does the std.cfg failure get written INTO the output file? Record exact stdout/stderr/exit for each. Key questions: is the std.cfg failure message ever reformatted/wrapped/redirected by these options? Does --output-file capture it? Also interactions with meta commands: --xml --errorlist (does errorlist change?), --output-file=X --errorlist (redirected?), --output-file=X --version, --output-file=X --help, --template=vs --errorlist. Record exact stdout/stderr/exit for every probe, and note which files got created with what content.

(2) Repetition and combination: --std=c11 --std=c99 (last wins? error?); --enable=warning --enable=style; -D FOO -D FOO; same file arg twice; --quiet --quiet. ec=$?

cat -A "$out"

cat -A "$err"

display.command:
D=/tmp/probe_output
run() { local label=$1; shift; (cd /workspace && ./executable.orig "$@" >"$D/$label.out" 2>"$D/$label.err"); echo "== $label exit=$? out=$(wc -c <"$D/$label.out")B err=$(wc -c <"$D/$label.err")B"; }
run xml --xml /tmp/probe_output/a.c
run of_text --output-format=text /tmp/probe_output/a.c
run of_sarif --output-format=sarif /tmp/probe_output/a.c
run of_xml --output-format=xml /tmp/probe_output/a.c
run of_xmlv2 --output-format=xmlv2 /tmp/probe_output/a.c
run of_xmlv3 --output-format=xmlv3 /tmp/probe_output/a.c
run of_bad --output-format=bad /tmp/probe_output/a.c
run xmlv2 --xml-version=2 /tmp/probe_output/a.c
run xmlv3 --xml-version=3 /tmp/probe_output/a.c
run xmlv_bad --xml-version=9 /tmp/probe_output/a.c
echo "=== DIFFS vs base ==="
for f in xml of_text of_sarif of_xml of_xmlv2 of_xmlv3 of_bad xmlv2 xmlv3 xmlv_bad; do
  cmp -s $D/base.out $D/$f.out && so=same || so=DIFF
  cmp -s $D/base.err $D/$f.err && se=same || se=DIFF
  echo "$f: stdout=$so stderr=$se"
done
for f in xml of_sarif of_bad xmlv_bad; do echo "--- $f.out"; cat -A $D/$f.out; echo "--- $f.err"; cat -A $D/$f.err; done

# Probe findings — AREA: analysis-paths (areaname: `analysis`)

Binary: `/workspace/executable.orig` ("cppcheck 2.19 dev"), invoked from `/workspace` as `./executable.orig`.
Environment: `/usr/local/share/Cppcheck/cfg/std.cfg` does not exist and must NOT be created.
All probes captured with `./executable.orig ARGS >/tmp/o 2>/tmp/e; echo exit=$?`, streams separated, bytes verified with `cat -A` / `wc -c`.

Test inputs created under `/tmp/probe_analysis/`:

- `empty.c` — 0 bytes
- `ok.c` — valid hello-world C
- `bad.c` — syntax-error C
- `unknown.txt` — valid C code, wrong extension
- `header.h` — a header
- `sub/` — contains `nested.c`, `nested.cpp`, `nested.h`
- `emptydir/` — empty directory
- `unreadable.c` — chmod 000 (note: probes run as root, so it is still readable by the process; irrelevant since files are never opened, see below)
- `broken.c` — symlink to nonexistent `does_not_exist.c`

## THE canonical failure message

Saved verbatim to `/workspace/probes/analysis_std_cfg_message.txt` (313 bytes, stdout). Exact content (line 1 = 107 chars + `\n`, line 2 = 231 chars + `\n`, total 313 bytes, no trailing whitespace, ends with a single newline):

```
cppcheck: Failed to load library configuration file 'std.cfg'. File not found
Failed to load std.cfg. Your Cppcheck installation is broken, please re-install. The Cppcheck binary was compiled with FILESDIR set to "/usr/local/share/Cppcheck" and will therefore search for std.cfg in /usr/local/share/Cppcheck/cfg.
```

This message goes to **stdout** (not stderr), stderr is empty, exit code is **1**.

## Group 1: input-type matrix — every analysis attempt is identical

All of the following produce **byte-identical output**: the 313-byte std.cfg message on stdout, empty stderr, exit 1. Verified with `cmp` against the baseline; no differences whatsoever (no "Checking ..." lines, no per-file output, nothing before or after the 2 lines).

| Command | exit | stdout | stderr |
|---|---|---|---|
| `./executable.orig /tmp/probe_analysis/empty.c` | 1 | std.cfg msg (313 B) | (empty) |
| `./executable.orig /tmp/probe_analysis/ok.c` | 1 | std.cfg msg | (empty) |
| `./executable.orig /tmp/probe_analysis/bad.c` | 1 | std.cfg msg | (empty) |
| `./executable.orig /tmp/probe_analysis/unknown.txt` | 1 | std.cfg msg | (empty) |
| `./executable.orig /tmp/probe_analysis/header.h` | 1 | std.cfg msg | (empty) |
| `./executable.orig /tmp/probe_analysis/sub` | 1 | std.cfg msg | (empty) |
| `./executable.orig /tmp/probe_analysis/sub/nested.c` | 1 | std.cfg msg | (empty) |
| `./executable.orig /tmp/probe_analysis/sub/nested.cpp` | 1 | std.cfg msg | (empty) |
| `./executable.orig /tmp/probe_analysis/emptydir` | 1 | std.cfg msg | (empty) |
| `./executable.orig /tmp/probe_analysis/unreadable.c` | 1 | std.cfg msg | (empty) |
| `./executable.orig /tmp/probe_analysis/broken.c` (broken symlink) | 1 | std.cfg msg | (empty) |
| `./executable.orig /tmp/probe_analysis/does_not_exist.c` (nonexistent) | 1 | std.cfg msg | (empty) |
| `./executable.orig /tmp/probe_analysis` (directory arg) | 1 | std.cfg msg | (empty) |
| `./executable.orig /tmp/probe_analysis/ok.c /tmp/probe_analysis/bad.c` (multiple) | 1 | std.cfg msg | (empty) |
| `./executable.orig /tmp/probe_analysis/ok.c /tmp/probe_analysis/ok.c` (same file twice) | 1 | std.cfg msg | (empty) |
| `./executable.orig /tmp/probe_analysis/ok.c /tmp/probe_analysis/unknown.txt` | 1 | std.cfg msg | (empty) |
| `./executable.orig ""` (empty-string positional) | 1 | std.cfg msg | (empty) |

Conclusion: the library (std.cfg) load happens BEFORE any path validation, extension filtering, file opening, or directory traversal. Nonexistent paths, unreadable files, broken symlinks, `.txt` files, and empty directories are all indistinguishable from valid inputs — they all reach the std.cfg load and die there.

### Exception: `-` as filename

```
$ ./executable.orig -
```
exit 1, stderr (empty), stdout (56 bytes):
```
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "-".
```

`-` is treated as an (invalid) option by the command-line parser, not as stdin. Piping data (`./executable.orig - < ok.c`) changes nothing — same 56-byte message. Likewise `--` alone is rejected:

```
$ ./executable.orig -- /tmp/probe_analysis/ok.c
```
exit 1, stderr (empty), stdout (57 bytes):
```
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--".
```

## Group 2: flags WITH ok.c — none of them change anything

Every one of the following was run as `./executable.orig FLAG /tmp/probe_analysis/ok.c`. **All** produced exactly the 313-byte std.cfg message on stdout, empty stderr, exit 1 (byte-identical, verified with `cmp`):

- `-E` — yes, even preprocessor-only mode still fails on std.cfg
- `--dump` — and NO `.dump` files are created anywhere (checked `/tmp/probe_analysis/` before/after; library load precedes dumping)
- `--check-config`
- `-q`, `--quiet` — failure output is NOT suppressed/shortened
- `-v`, `--verbose` — no extra output is added
- `--quiet --verbose` together — still identical
- `-j 2`, `-j2`, `-j 4 ok.c bad.c sub` (multithreaded, multiple inputs)
- `-D FOO`, `-DFOO=1`, `-U FOO`, `-I /tmp`, `-i /tmp/probe_analysis`
- `-x c`, `-x c++`, `--language=c`
- `--file-filter='*.c'`, `--file-filter='*'`, `--file-filter='*' unknown.txt`
- `--safety`, `--inline-suppr`, `--inconclusive`, `--force`, `-f`
- `--max-configs=1`
- `--showtime=summary`, `--showtime=file` — no timing lines appear before the failure
- `--report-progress` — nothing
- `--relative-paths`
- `--error-exitcode=5` — **exit code stays 1**; the std.cfg failure exit code is hardcoded and ignores `--error-exitcode`
- `--error-exitcode=0` — exit still 1
- `--error-exitcode=5 ok.c bad.c` (multi-file) — exit still 1

## Group 3: parser errors take precedence over the std.cfg failure

Command-line parsing/validation happens FIRST. Any parse error short-circuits before the "no source files" check and before the library load. All parse errors share this shape: printed on **stdout** (stderr always empty), exit **1**, format `cppcheck: error: <message>` ending with a newline, order of arguments irrelevant (file-first or flag-first gives the same result).

```
$ ./executable.orig --bogus-flag /tmp/probe_analysis/ok.c     # or: ok.c --bogus-flag
```
exit 1, stderr (empty), stdout (67 bytes):
```
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--bogus-flag".
```

```
$ ./executable.orig --std=bad /tmp/probe_analysis/ok.c        # or: ok.c --std=bad
```
exit 1, stderr (empty), stdout (43 bytes):
```
cppcheck: error: unknown --std value 'bad'
```
(Note: this one has NO trailing period, unlike the others.)

```
$ ./executable.orig /tmp/probe_analysis/ok.c -j    # same for -D, -U, -I, -i
```
exit 1, stderr (empty), stdout (46 bytes):
```
cppcheck: error: argument to '-j' is missing.
```
The exact strings for the other options: `cppcheck: error: argument to '-D' is missing.`, `... '-U' ...`, `... '-I' ...`, `... '-i' ...` (all 46 bytes + newline pattern).

```
$ ./executable.orig --error-exitcode=abc /tmp/probe_analysis/ok.c
```
exit 1, stderr (empty), stdout (80 bytes):
```
cppcheck: error: argument to '--error-exitcode=' is not valid - not an integer.
```

```
$ ./executable.orig -j0 /tmp/probe_analysis/ok.c
```
exit 1, stderr (empty), stdout (59 bytes):
```
cppcheck: error: argument for '-j' must be greater than 0.
```
(Note: "argument for" here vs "argument to" in the missing/not-an-integer variants.)

```
$ ./executable.orig -j foo /tmp/probe_analysis/ok.c
```
exit 1, stderr (empty), stdout (65 bytes):
```
cppcheck: error: argument to '-j' is not valid - not an integer.
```

```
$ ./executable.orig --max-configs=0 /tmp/probe_analysis/ok.c
```
exit 1, stderr (empty), stdout (70 bytes):
```
cppcheck: error: argument to '--max-configs=' must be greater than 0.
```

```
$ ./executable.orig --showtime=bogus /tmp/probe_analysis/ok.c
```
exit 1, stderr (empty), stdout (125 bytes):
```
cppcheck: error: unrecognized --showtime mode: 'bogus'. Supported modes: file, file-total, summary, top5_file, top5_summary.
```

```
$ ./executable.orig -x fortran /tmp/probe_analysis/ok.c
```
exit 1, stderr (empty), stdout (54 bytes):
```
cppcheck: error: unknown language 'fortran' enforced.
```

## Group 4: flags but NO positional argument — "no source files"

When parsing succeeds but there are zero positional arguments (and no early-exit flag like `--help`/`--version`/`--errorlist`), the std.cfg load is never reached either. All of these: exit 1, stderr (empty), stdout (49 bytes):

```
cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.
```

Produced identically by: `-q`, `-v`, `--quiet`, `-E`, `-j 2`, `--check-config`, `--dump`, `--safety`, `--language=c`, `-i /tmp/probe_analysis` (all with no positional arg).

Note the subtlety: an empty-string positional `""`, a nonexistent path, a `.txt` file, or an empty directory DO count as "a positional argument" and proceed to the std.cfg failure instead. The "no source files" check appears to be purely "was at least one positional path given", with all real path/extension validation deferred until after the (never-survived) library load.

## KEY RULES

1. **Strict precedence pipeline** (first failure wins, all exit 1):
   1. Command-line parse/validation errors → `cppcheck: error: <specific message>` on stdout.
   2. Zero positional arguments → `cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.` on stdout.
   3. Library load (std.cfg) → the 2-line 313-byte message on stdout. In this environment, step 3 ALWAYS fails, so steps after it are unreachable.
2. **Everything goes to stdout.** stderr was 0 bytes in every single probe, including all error cases. There is no error output on stderr ever.
3. **The std.cfg failure is all-or-nothing and pre-empts everything downstream**: no path validation, no extension filtering, no file opening, no directory traversal, no "Checking ..." progress, no preprocessing (`-E`), no dumps (`--dump` creates nothing), no timing (`--showtime=*`), no per-file messages. Before the 2 lines, NOTHING is printed, under any flag.
4. **Exit code is hardwired to 1** for the std.cfg failure: `--error-exitcode=5` and even `--error-exitcode=0` do not change it. Parser errors and the no-files error are also exit 1.
5. **Quiet/verbose are no-ops for this failure**: `-q`, `--quiet`, `-v`, `--verbose`, and both together produce byte-identical output.
6. **Input existence/type is irrelevant**: valid C, broken C, empty file, header, `.txt`, directory, empty directory, nonexistent path, broken symlink, unreadable file, duplicates, and multiple inputs all yield the identical 313-byte stdout message.
7. **`-` and `--` are not special**: both are rejected as `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "%1%".` (with the literal token substituted). There is no stdin mode reachable via `-`.
8. **Message formats** (all on stdout, single trailing `\n`):
   - Unrecognized option: `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "%1%".`
   - Unknown std: `cppcheck: error: unknown --std value '%1%'` (NO trailing period)
   - Missing option argument: `cppcheck: error: argument to '%1%' is missing.`
   - Bad integer: `cppcheck: error: argument to '%1%' is not valid - not an integer.`
   - Non-positive: `cppcheck: error: argument for '-j' must be greater than 0.` / `cppcheck: error: argument to '--max-configs=' must be greater than 0.` (note "for" vs "to")
   - Bad showtime: `cppcheck: error: unrecognized --showtime mode: '%1%'. Supported modes: file, file-total, summary, top5_file, top5_summary.`
   - Bad enforced language: `cppcheck: error: unknown language '%1%' enforced.`
   - No files: `cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.`
   - std.cfg failure (2 lines, verbatim in `/workspace/probes/analysis_std_cfg_message.txt`):
     `cppcheck: Failed to load library configuration file 'std.cfg'. File not found`
     `Failed to load std.cfg. Your Cppcheck installation is broken, please re-install. The Cppcheck binary was compiled with FILESDIR set to "/usr/local/share/Cppcheck" and will therefore search for std.cfg in /usr/local/share/Cppcheck/cfg.`
9. **"No source files" trigger is positional-count only**: any positional token (even `""`, nonexistent, or wrong-extension) suppresses the no-files error and proceeds to the std.cfg failure.

1. **Strict precedence pipeline** (first failure wins, all exit 1):
   1. Command-line parse/validation errors → `cppcheck: error: <specific message>` on stdout.
   2. Zero positional arguments → `cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.` on stdout.
   3. Library load (std.cfg) → the 2-line 313-byte message on stdout. In this environment, step 3 ALWAYS fails, so steps after it are unreachable.
2. **Everything goes to stdout.** stderr was 0 bytes in every single probe, including all error cases. There is no error output on stderr ever.
3. **The std.cfg failure is all-or-nothing and pre-empts everything downstream**: no path validation, no extension filtering, no file opening, no directory traversal, no "Checking ..." progress, no preprocessing (`-E`), no dumps (`--dump` creates nothing), no timing (`--showtime=*`), no per-file messages. Before the 2 lines, NOTHING is printed, under any flag.
4. **Exit code is hardwired to 1** for the std.cfg failure: `--error-exitcode=5` and even `--error-exitcode=0` do not change it. Parser errors and the no-files error are also exit 1.
5. **Quiet/verbose are no-ops for this failure**: `-q`, `--quiet`, `-v`, `--verbose`, and both together produce byte-identical output.

7. **`-` and `--` are not special**: both are rejected as `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "%1%".` (with the literal token substituted). There is no stdin mode reachable via `-`.
8. **Message formats** (all on stdout, single trailing `\n`):
   - Unrecognized option: `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "%1%".`
   - Unknown std: `cppcheck: error: unknown --std value '%1%'` (NO trailing period)
   - Missing option argument: `cppcheck: error: argument to '%1%' is missing.`
   - Bad integer: `cppcheck: error: argument to '%1%' is not valid - not an integer.`
   - Non-positive: `cppcheck: error: argument for '-j' must be greater than 0.` / `cppcheck: error: argument to '--max-configs=' must be greater than 0.` (note "for" vs "to")
   - Bad showtime: `cppcheck: error: unrecognized --showtime mode: '%1%'. Supported modes: file, file-total, summary, top5_file, top5_summary.`
   - Bad enforced language: `cppcheck: error: unknown language '%1%' enforced.`
   - No files: `cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.`
   - std.cfg failure (2 lines, verbatim in `/workspace/probes/analysis_std_cfg_message.txt`):
     `cppcheck: Failed to load library configuration file 'std.cfg'. File not found`

payload.resultSummary:
Report written to `/workspace/probes/analysis.md` (plus the verbatim 313-byte message at `/workspace/probes/analysis_std_cfg_message.txt`). Summary of key findings:

1. **Every** analysis attempt — valid/broken/empty C, headers, `.txt`, directories, empty dirs, nonexistent paths, broken symlinks, unreadable files, duplicates, multi-file — produces byte-identical output: the 2-line 313-byte std.cfg failure on **stdout**, exit 1.
2. stderr was 0 bytes in **all** ~60 probes, including every error case — all diagnostics route to stdout.
3. The std.cfg load precedes all path validation, extension filtering, file I/O, and traversal — so no input is distinguishable from any other.
4. `-E` still fails; `--dump` creates zero files; `--showtime=*`, `--report-progress`, `-v` print nothing before the failure; no "Checking ..." lines ever.
5. `--error-exitcode=5` (and even `=0`) does **not** change the exit code — the std.cfg failure is hardwired to exit 1.
6. `-q`/`--quiet`/`-v`/`--verbose`/both together are no-ops for the failure output.
7. Precedence: parser errors → "no source files" (zero positionals) → std.cfg failure (always fatal here).
8. `-` and `--` are both rejected as `unrecognized command line option: "%1%".` — no stdin mode.
9. The "no C or C++ source files found." error (49 bytes) triggers only on zero positional args; even `""`, nonexistent, or wrong-extension positionals proceed to the std.cfg failure.
10. Parser-error formats captured verbatim, including quirks: `--std` error has no trailing period, `-j0` says "argument for" while others say "argument to", and `--showtime=bogus` lists the 5 supported modes.

# AREA: meta-outputs (`-h`, `--help`, `--version`, `--errorlist`, no-args)

Binary: `/workspace/executable.orig` ("Cppcheck 2.19 dev"), execute-only.
All probes run from `/workspace` as `./executable.orig ARGS >/tmp/o 2>/tmp/e; echo exit=$?`.
Scratch file used where a file argument was needed: `/tmp/probe_1201/t.c` containing `int main(){return 0;}`.

## Large deterministic outputs (saved files, verified byte-identical to fresh captures)

| Output | File | Size (bytes) | Exit | Stream |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--help` / `-h` / no-args | `/workspace/probes/help.stdout.txt` | 20176 | 0 | stdout only |
| `--version` | `/workspace/probes/version.stdout.txt` | 18 | 0 | stdout only |
| `--errorlist` | `/workspace/probes/errorlist.stdout.txt` | 105141 | 0 | stdout only |

- `cmp` confirmed: no-args stdout == `-h` stdout == `--help` stdout == `help.stdout.txt` (byte-for-byte).
- `--version` stdout is exactly `Cppcheck 2.19 dev\n` (18 bytes, single trailing LF).
- `--errorlist` stdout is one XML document, 105141 bytes, contains 338 `<error id=` elements.
  - Head (od-verified): `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>\n<results version="2">\n    <cppcheck version="2.19 dev"/>\n    <errors>` — **QUIRK: there is NO newline after `<errors>`**; the first `<error .../>` element begins on the same line immediately after `<errors>` (8 spaces indent before `<errors>`, then 8 spaces before the first `<error>`).
  - Tail ends with: `        <error id="nonStandardCharLiteral" severity="portability" msg="Non-standard character literal. " verbose="Non-standard character literal. "/>\n    </errors>\n</results>\n` (single trailing LF).
- All three outputs have EMPTY stderr in every probe below unless stated otherwise.

## Baseline meta invocations

```
./executable.orig
exit=0
stdout: (20176 bytes == help.stdout.txt)
stderr: (empty)

./executable.orig -h
exit=0
stdout: (identical to help.stdout.txt)
stderr: (empty)

./executable.orig --help
exit=0
stdout: (identical to help.stdout.txt)
stderr: (empty)

./executable.orig --version
exit=0
stdout:
Cppcheck 2.19 dev
stderr: (empty)

./executable.orig --errorlist
exit=0
stdout: (105141 bytes == errorlist.stdout.txt)
stderr: (empty)
```

## Meta flag + extra arguments (files, valid flags) — meta always wins, output identical to baseline

All of the following produced exit=0, empty stderr, and stdout byte-identical to the corresponding baseline (help 20176 / version 18 / errorlist 105141):

```
./executable.orig --help /tmp/probe_1201/t.c        -> help
./executable.orig -h /tmp/probe_1201/t.c            -> help
./executable.orig /tmp/probe_1201/t.c --help        -> help
./executable.orig --version /tmp/probe_1201/t.c     -> version
./executable.orig /tmp/probe_1201/t.c --version     -> version
./executable.orig --errorlist /tmp/probe_1201/t.c   -> errorlist
./executable.orig /tmp/probe_1201/t.c --errorlist   -> errorlist
./executable.orig -q --version                      -> version
./executable.orig --version -q                      -> version
./executable.orig --version --version               -> version
```

So analysis is never attempted when a meta flag is present; no std.cfg failure appears.

## Meta flag + INVALID arguments — meta still wins (parse errors suppressed)

All exit=0, stderr empty:

```
./executable.orig --bogus --help      -> help    (byte-identical to help.stdout.txt)
./executable.orig --help --bogus      -> help
./executable.orig --bogus --version   -> version
./executable.orig --version --bogus   -> version
./executable.orig --bogus --errorlist -> errorlist
./executable.orig --errorlist --bogus -> errorlist
./executable.orig --std=bad --help    -> help
./executable.orig --help --std=bad    -> help
./executable.orig --std=bad --version -> version
./executable.orig --version --std=bad -> version
./executable.orig --errorlist --std=bad            -> errorlist
./executable.orig --std=bad --errorlist            -> errorlist
./executable.orig --std=bad t.c --errorlist        -> errorlist
./executable.orig --errorlist --suppressions-list=/nonexistent.txt -> errorlist
./executable.orig -- --help           -> help    (!! see `--` notes below)
./executable.orig --errorlist --version t.c --bogus -> errorlist
```

Even an unrecognized option or an invalid `--std` value that appears BEFORE the meta flag produces no error at all.

## Precedence AMONG meta flags: FIRST meta flag in argv order wins

The set of meta flags is exactly `-h`, `--help`, `--version`, `--errorlist`. The first one on the command line determines the output; later ones are ignored. All exit=0, stderr empty:

```
./executable.orig -h --version            -> help (20176)
./executable.orig --version -h            -> version (18)
./executable.orig --help --errorlist      -> help
./executable.orig --errorlist --help      -> errorlist
./executable.orig --version --errorlist   -> version
./executable.orig --errorlist --version   -> errorlist
./executable.orig -h --version --errorlist -> help
./executable.orig --errorlist --version -h -> errorlist
```

## --errorlist output is INVARIANT under configuration flags

Each of the following produced stdout byte-identical (`cmp`-verified) to `errorlist.stdout.txt`, exit=0, stderr empty:

```
./executable.orig --errorlist --enable=all
./executable.orig --errorlist --disable=style
./executable.orig --errorlist --inconclusive
./executable.orig --errorlist --xml
./executable.orig --errorlist --xml --xml-version=2
./executable.orig --errorlist --output-format=sarif
./executable.orig --errorlist --output-format=text
./executable.orig --errorlist --std=c11
./executable.orig --errorlist --platform=unix64
./executable.orig --errorlist -DX
./executable.orig --errorlist -q
./executable.orig --errorlist --max-configs=5
./executable.orig --errorlist --enable=all --inconclusive --std=c++20 --platform=win64
```

`--enable`/`--disable`/`--std`/`--platform`/`--xml`/`--output-format`/`--inconclusive` do NOT filter or reformat the error list. It is always the same static XML.

## --output-file is IGNORED by meta outputs

```
./executable.orig --errorlist --output-file=/tmp/probe_1201/outfile.txt
exit=0
stdout: full errorlist XML (105141 bytes)
stderr: (empty)
side effect: /tmp/probe_1201/outfile.txt was NOT created

./executable.orig --version --output-file=/tmp/probe_1201/outfile2.txt
exit=0
stdout: Cppcheck 2.19 dev
stderr: (empty)
side effect: outfile2.txt NOT created
```

Meta output always goes to real stdout regardless of `--output-file`.

## Exact meta-flag spelling — no variants accepted

Each of these is exit=1, stderr empty, stdout is the unrecognized-option error (62-ish bytes, format below):

```
./executable.orig --HELP
stdout:
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--HELP".

./executable.orig --Version
stdout:
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--Version".

./executable.orig -help
stdout:
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "-help".

./executable.orig --help=foo
stdout:
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--help=foo".

./executable.orig --version=x
stdout:
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--version=x".

./executable.orig --errorlist=x
stdout:
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--errorlist=x".

./executable.orig -qh
stdout:
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "-qh".
```

Flags are case-sensitive, single-dash long forms are rejected, `=value` attachments on meta flags are rejected, short flags are not combinable (`-qh` is one unrecognized token).

## `--` and `-` handling

```
./executable.orig --
exit=1
stdout:
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--".
stderr: (empty)

./executable.orig -- /tmp/probe_1201/t.c
exit=1
stdout:
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--".

./executable.orig -- --bogus
exit=1
stdout:
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--".

./executable.orig -
exit=1
stdout:
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "-".
```

So `--` is NOT an end-of-options separator — it is itself an unrecognized option (and, per the earlier probe, `-- --help` still prints help because a meta flag anywhere overrides the error).

## Error messages: formats, stream routing, exit codes

All CLI errors observed go to **stdout** (never stderr), end with a single `\n`, and exit code is **1**:

```
./executable.orig --bogus
exit=1, stderr=(empty), stdout (62 bytes, cat -A):
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--bogus".$
```
Format: `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "%1%".` — double quotes around the verbatim offending token, trailing PERIOD, then LF. (61 chars + LF.)

```
./executable.orig --std=bad
exit=1, stderr=(empty), stdout (43 bytes):
cppcheck: error: unknown --std value 'bad'$
```
Format: `cppcheck: error: unknown --std value '%1%'` — single quotes, NO trailing period, then LF.

```
./executable.orig -q            (also --enable=all, -D X, --xml, --inconclusive,
exit=1                            --std=c11, --platform=unix64, -v — any valid
stderr: (empty)                   flags but no file arguments)
stdout (49 bytes):
cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.$
```
Format: `cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.` — trailing PERIOD. Any invocation with at least one argument but no input file/path yields this; it never reaches the std.cfg failure (file-discovery emptiness is detected first).

### Error precedence among multiple bad options: FIRST failing option in argv order wins

```
./executable.orig --bad1 --bad2
stdout: cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--bad1".

./executable.orig --std=bad --bogus
stdout: cppcheck: error: unknown --std value 'bad'

./executable.orig --bogus --std=bad
stdout: cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--bogus".
```

---

## KEY RULES

1. **Meta-flag set**: exactly `-h`, `--help`, `--version`, `--errorlist`. Exact spelling required (case-sensitive; no `=value`; no single-dash long forms; short flags don't combine).
2. **Meta precedence over everything**: if any meta flag appears anywhere on the command line, the FIRST meta flag in argv order is executed: its output is printed to stdout and the process exits 0. All other arguments — files, valid options, invalid options, bad `--std` values, `--` — are completely ignored; no parse errors, no analysis, no std.cfg failure.
3. **Meta outputs**:
   - help (`-h`/`--help`/no-args): 20176 bytes, fixed text, stdout, exit 0. See `/workspace/probes/help.stdout.txt`.
   - `--version`: exactly `Cppcheck 2.19 dev\n` (18 bytes), stdout, exit 0.
   - `--errorlist`: 105141-byte static XML, stdout, exit 0. See `/workspace/probes/errorlist.stdout.txt`. **Invariant** under `--enable`/`--disable`/`--std`/`--platform`/`--xml`/`--output-format`/`--inconclusive`/etc. Quirk: no newline between `<errors>` and the first `<error .../>` element.
4. **No-args == help**: zero arguments prints the help text to stdout, exit 0 (byte-identical to `--help`).
5. **Flags but no files**: one or more valid non-meta arguments with no input file/path -> `cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.` on stdout, exit 1. This fires BEFORE any std.cfg loading; help is only printed when argc==1 (or a meta flag present).
6. **Stream routing**: EVERYTHING — help, version, errorlist, and all CLI error messages — goes to **stdout**. stderr is always empty in every probed scenario.
7. **Exit codes**: meta outputs -> 0. Any CLI parse/usage error -> 1.
8. **Error formats** (each followed by exactly one `\n`):
   - `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "%1%".` (double quotes, trailing period; %1% = the exact offending argv token)
   - `cppcheck: error: unknown --std value '%1%'` (single quotes, NO trailing period)
   - `cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.` (trailing period)
9. **Error precedence**: with multiple bad options, the first one in argv order is reported; only one error is printed.
10. **`--` is not special**: it is treated as an unrecognized option token itself; `-` likewise.
11. **`--output-file` is ignored** by meta outputs: output always goes to real stdout, no file is created.

```

So `--` is NOT an end-of-options separator — it is itself an unrecognized option (and, per the earlier probe, `-- --help` still prints help because a meta flag anywhere overrides the error).

## Error messages: formats, stream routing, exit codes

All CLI errors observed go to **stdout** (never stderr), end with a single `\n`, and exit code is **1**:

```

exit=1, stderr=(empty), stdout (62 bytes, cat -A):
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--bogus".$
```
Format: `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "%1%".` — double quotes around the verbatim offending token, trailing PERIOD, then LF. (61 chars + LF.)

```

exit=1, stderr=(empty), stdout (43 bytes):
cppcheck: error: unknown --std value 'bad'$
```
Format: `cppcheck: error: unknown --std value '%1%'` — single quotes, NO trailing period, then LF.

```

exit=1                            --std=c11, --platform=unix64, -v — any valid
stderr: (empty)                   flags but no file arguments)
stdout (49 bytes):
cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.$
```
Format: `cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.` — trailing PERIOD. Any invocation with at least one argument but no input file/path yields this; it never reaches the std.cfg failure (file-discovery emptiness is detected first).

### Error precedence among multiple bad options: FIRST failing option in argv order wins

```
./executable.orig --bad1 --bad2
stdout: cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--bad1".

./executable.orig --std=bad --bogus
stdout: cppcheck: error: unknown --std value 'bad'

./executable.orig --bogus --std=bad
stdout: cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--bogus".
```

---

## KEY RULES

1. **Meta-flag set**: exactly `-h`, `--help`, `--version`, `--errorlist`. Exact spelling required (case-sensitive; no `=value`; no single-dash long forms; short flags don't combine).
2. **Meta precedence over everything**: if any meta flag appears anywhere on the command line, the FIRST meta flag in argv order is executed: its output is printed to stdout and the process exits 0. All other arguments — files, valid options, invalid options, bad `--std` values, `--` — are completely ignored; no parse errors, no analysis, no std.cfg failure.
3. **Meta outputs**:
   - help (`-h`/`--help`/no-args): 20176 bytes, fixed text, stdout, exit 0. See `/workspace/probes/help.stdout.txt`.
   - `--version`: exactly `Cppcheck 2.19 dev\n` (18 bytes), stdout, exit 0.
   - `--errorlist`: 105141-byte static XML, stdout, exit 0. See `/workspace/probes/errorlist.stdout.txt`. **Invariant** under `--enable`/`--disable`/`--std`/`--platform`/`--xml`/`--output-format`/`--inconclusive`/etc. Quirk: no newline between `<errors>` and the first `<error .../>` element.
4. **No-args == help**: zero arguments prints the help text to stdout, exit 0 (byte-identical to `--help`).
5. **Flags but no files**: one or more valid non-meta arguments with no input file/path -> `cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.` on stdout, exit 1. This fires BEFORE any std.cfg loading; help is only printed when argc==1 (or a meta flag present).
6. **Stream routing**: EVERYTHING — help, version, errorlist, and all CLI error messages — goes to **stdout**. stderr is always empty in every probed scenario.
7. **Exit codes**: meta outputs -> 0. Any CLI parse/usage error -> 1.
8. **Error formats** (each followed by exactly one `\n`):
   - `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "%1%".` (double quotes, trailing period; %1% = the exact offending argv token)
   - `cppcheck: error: unknown --std value '%1%'` (single quotes, NO trailing period)
   - `cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.` (trailing period)
9. **Error precedence**: with multiple bad options, the first one in argv order is reported; only one error is printed.
10. **`--` is not special**: it is treated as an unrecognized option token itself; `-` likewise.
11. **`--output-file` is ignored** by meta outputs: output always goes to real stdout, no file is created.

Report written to `/workspace/probes/meta.md`. 10-line summary of key findings:

1. **Meta flags override everything**: `-h`/`--help`/`--version`/`--errorlist` anywhere on the command line — even after `--bogus`, `--std=bad`, or `--` — suppress all errors and analysis, print their output, exit 0 (`--bogus --help` → help, no error).
2. **Among meta flags, first-in-argv-order wins**: `--version -h` → version; `-h --version` → help; `--errorlist --version` → errorlist.
3. **`--errorlist` output is fully static**: byte-identical (105141 B) under `--enable=all`, `--disable`, `--std`, `--platform`, `--xml`, `--output-format=sarif`, `--inconclusive`, `-D`, etc.
4. **errorlist XML quirk**: no newline after `<errors>` — the first `<error .../>` starts on the same line; 338 error ids; ends `</errors>\n</results>\n`.
5. **Everything routes to stdout** — help, version, errorlist, and all error messages; stderr is always empty.
6. **All CLI errors exit 1**; meta outputs exit 0.
7. **Flags-but-no-files** (e.g. `-q`, `--enable=all`, `--xml` alone) → `cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.` on stdout exit 1 — never reaching the std.cfg failure; help is printed only when argc==1.
8. **Error formats differ subtly**: unrecognized option uses double quotes + trailing period (`...option: "--bogus".`); unknown --std uses single quotes, NO period (`unknown --std value 'bad'`).
9. **With multiple bad options, only the first in argv order is reported**; unrecognized-option check and --std validation appear to happen in a single left-to-right parse, overruled afterwards by any meta flag.
10. **Edge cases**: `--` and `-` are themselves unrecognized options (no end-of-options semantics); meta flags reject `=value`, single-dash long forms, wrong case, and combined shorts (`-qh`); `--output-file` is ignored by meta outputs (no file created).

args.content:
# AREA: templates-and-output (areaname: `output`)

Binary: `/workspace/executable.orig` (cppcheck 2.19 dev), run from `/workspace`.
Target file: `/tmp/probe_output/a.c` containing `int main(){int x; return x;}`.
Convention: `./executable.orig ARGS >/tmp/o 2>/tmp/e; echo exit=$?`. All byte counts verified with `wc -c` / `cat -A` / `cmp`.

**Universal observation: in every single probe below, stderr was EMPTY (0 bytes). Everything — normal output, parse errors, the std.cfg failure — goes to stdout only.**

## 0. Baseline (reference for all comparisons)

Command: `./executable.orig /tmp/probe_output/a.c`
Exit: **1**. Stdout (313 bytes, exactly, `$` = newline):

```
cppcheck: Failed to load library configuration file 'std.cfg'. File not found$
Failed to load std.cfg. Your Cppcheck installation is broken, please re-install. The Cppcheck binary was compiled with FILESDIR set to "/usr/local/share/Cppcheck" and will therefore search for std.cfg in /usr/local/share/Cppcheck/cfg.$
```

Stderr: (empty). Both lines end with `\n`; no trailing spaces. Only the first line has the `cppcheck: ` prefix (and note: `cppcheck: Failed...`, NOT `cppcheck: error: ...`).

## 1. --template with analysis: NO EFFECT on the std.cfg failure

Every one of these commands produced exit 1, stdout byte-identical to the baseline (313 B), stderr empty:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `./executable.orig --template=gcc /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | == baseline |
| `./executable.orig --template=cppcheck1 /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | == baseline |
| `./executable.orig --template=vs /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | == baseline |
| `./executable.orig --template=edit /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | == baseline |
| `./executable.orig --template='{file}:{line}:{severity}:{id}:{message}' /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | == baseline |
| `./executable.orig --template='' /tmp/probe_output/a.c` (empty value) | == baseline |
| `./executable.orig --template='{bogus}' /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | == baseline |
| `./executable.orig --template='{' /tmp/probe_output/a.c` (unclosed brace) | == baseline |
| `./executable.orig --template=$'{file}\\t{line}\\n{message}' /tmp/probe_output/a.c` (literal backslash-t/-n in arg) | == baseline |
| `./executable.orig --template=bogusname /tmp/probe_output/a.c` (unknown predefined name) | == baseline |

No validation of template names/placeholders happens before the std.cfg failure; nothing is reformatted.

## 2. --template-location with analysis: NO EFFECT

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `./executable.orig --template-location='{file}:{line}: note: {info}' /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | exit 1, == baseline, stderr empty |
| `./executable.orig --template-location='{' /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | exit 1, == baseline, stderr empty |
| `./executable.orig --template-location= --template= /tmp/probe_output/a.c` (both empty) | exit 1, == baseline, stderr empty |

## 3. --xml / --output-format / --xml-version with analysis

These all produced exit 1, stdout byte-identical to baseline (313 B), stderr empty — the failure message is NOT wrapped in XML/SARIF, not templated, not suppressed:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `--xml /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | == baseline |
| `--output-format=text /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | == baseline |
| `--output-format=sarif /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | == baseline |
| `--output-format=xml /tmp/probe_output/a.c` (deprecated alias; NO deprecation warning printed) | == baseline |
| `--output-format=xmlv2 /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | == baseline |
| `--output-format=xmlv3 /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | == baseline |
| `--xml-version=2 /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | == baseline (so `--xml-version` IS recognized; valid values 2 and 3) |
| `--xml-version=3 /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | == baseline |
| `--xml --xml-version=2 /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | == baseline |
| `--xml --xml-version=3 /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | == baseline |
| `--output-format=text --output-format=sarif /tmp/probe_output/a.c` (repeated) | == baseline (last wins, no error) |
| `--xml --template=vs --output-file=/tmp/probe_output/o.txt /tmp/probe_output/a.c` (all combined) | == baseline; o.txt NOT created |

### Invalid values → parse-time errors (stdout, exit 1, stderr empty)

`./executable.orig --output-format=bad /tmp/probe_output/a.c` (same for `--output-format=XML`, `=TEXT` — case-sensitive — and `--output-format=` empty):
```
cppcheck: error: argument to '--output-format=' must be 'text', 'sarif', 'xml' (deprecated), 'xmlv2' or 'xmlv3'.$
```

`./executable.orig --xml-version=9 /tmp/probe_output/a.c` (integer but not 2/3):
```
cppcheck: error: '--xml-version' can only be 2 or 3.$
```

`./executable.orig --xml-version=abc /tmp/probe_output/a.c` (also `=2x`, `=` empty):
```
cppcheck: error: argument to '--xml-version=' is not valid - not an integer.$
```

## 4. --output-file: NEVER captures or redirects the std.cfg failure

| Command | Exit | Stdout | Out-file |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--output-file=/tmp/probe_output/out.txt /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | 1 | == baseline (313 B) | **NOT created** |
| `--xml --output-file=.../out.txt /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | 1 | == baseline | **NOT created** |
| `--template=vs --output-file=.../out.txt /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | 1 | == baseline | **NOT created** |
| `--output-format=sarif --output-file=.../out.txt /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | 1 | == baseline | **NOT created** |
| `--output-file= /tmp/probe_output/a.c` (empty value) | 1 | == baseline | n/a (accepted silently) |
| `--output-file=.../out.txt` (no input files) | 1 | see below | NOT created |

`--output-file=.../out.txt` with no files, stdout (49 B):
```
cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.$
```
(Bare `./executable.orig` with no args prints the full 20176-byte help, exit 0 — but as soon as any non-meta option is present, missing files is an error.)

## 5. Meta commands are completely immune to output options

Reference outputs saved: `/workspace/probes/errorlist.xml` (105141 B, exit 0) and `/workspace/probes/help.txt` (20176 B, exit 0). `--version` = `Cppcheck 2.19 dev\n` (18 B, exit 0).

All of these are **byte-identical** to the plain meta command, exit 0, stderr empty, and `--output-file` target is **never created**:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `--xml --errorlist` | == `--errorlist` |
| `--output-format=xmlv3 --errorlist` | == `--errorlist` |
| `--output-format=sarif --errorlist` | == `--errorlist` |
| `--xml-version=3 --errorlist` | == `--errorlist` |
| `--template=vs --errorlist` | == `--errorlist` |
| `--output-file=/tmp/probe_output/out.txt --errorlist` | == `--errorlist`; out.txt NOT created (NOT redirected) |
| `--output-file=.../out.txt --version` | `Cppcheck 2.19 dev`; out.txt NOT created |
| `--template=gcc --version` | `Cppcheck 2.19 dev` |
| `--output-file=.../out.txt --help` | == `--help`; out.txt NOT created |
| `--xml --help` | == `--help` |
| `--errorlist /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | == `--errorlist` (input files ignored) |
| `--version /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | `Cppcheck 2.19 dev` |

`--errorlist` output begins `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>` / `<results version="2">` / `    <cppcheck version="2.19 dev"/>` regardless of `--xml`/`--output-format`/`--xml-version` — it is always the same fixed XML v2 document.

## 6. Precedence: meta commands beat ALL parse errors; first meta wins

Every command below exits **0** with the meta output on stdout, stderr empty — the parse error is silently discarded:

| Command | Output |
|---|---|
| `--output-format=bad --version` | version |
| `--version --output-format=bad` | version |
| `--output-format=bad --errorlist` | errorlist |
| `--xml-version=9 --errorlist` | errorlist |
| `--std=bad --errorlist` | errorlist |
| `--bogus-flag --errorlist` | errorlist (unknown option BEFORE meta still discarded!) |
| `--errorlist --bogus-flag` | errorlist |
| `--help --bogus-flag` | help |
| `--bogus-flag --help` | help |

Meta vs meta — **the FIRST meta flag on the command line wins**:

| Command | Output |
|---|---|
| `--version --errorlist` | version |
| `--errorlist --version` | errorlist |
| `--help --version` | help |
| `--version --help` | version |
| `--help --errorlist` | help |
| `--errorlist --help` | errorlist |

Consistent model: argument parsing scans left to right; encountering `--help`/`--version`/`--errorlist` prints and exits 0 IMMEDIATELY. Value/unknown-option errors are DEFERRED (collected during the scan, reported only if parsing completes without hitting a meta flag) — which is why `--bogus-flag --errorlist` still prints the errorlist.

## 7. Space-separated option forms are NOT accepted (area options require `=`)

Each of these exits 1, stderr empty, stdout:
| Command | Stdout |
|---|---|
| `--template gcc /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--template".$` |
| `--template-location '{file}' /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--template-location".$` |
| `--output-file X /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--output-file".$` |
| `--output-format text /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--output-format".$` |
| `--xml-version 2 /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--xml-version".$` |
| bare `--template` / `--output-file` etc. (no `=`) | same "unrecognized" message |

Also: `-` as an argument → `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "-".$` exit 1 (no stdin reading in this build).

## KEY RULES

1. **The std.cfg failure is raw and unformattable.** It is always exactly the two baseline lines (313 B) on **stdout**, exit 1, and is emitted before/around any output machinery: `--template` (any value incl. empty, `{bogus}`, `{`, unknown names), `--template-location`, `--xml`, `--output-format=*` (all 5 valid values), `--xml-version=2|3`, and `--output-file` have ZERO effect on it. No XML/SARIF wrapping, no templating, no redirection.
2. **`--output-file` never captures anything in this broken-install state.** With analysis it is never even created (failure happens first); with meta commands (`--errorlist`/`--version`/`--help`) it is also ignored — output stays on stdout and the file is not created.
3. **Stream routing: everything on stdout, always.** Parse errors (`cppcheck: error: ...`), the std.cfg failure (`cppcheck: Failed...` — note: no `error:` infix on line 1), and all meta output go to stdout. stderr was 0 bytes in every probe.
4. **Meta precedence:** `--help`, `--version`, `--errorlist` act immediately when encountered during the left-to-right arg scan (print to stdout, exit 0). They therefore beat ANY parse error no matter where the error appears (`--bogus-flag --errorlist` → errorlist, exit 0). Among multiple meta flags, the FIRST one wins. Input files are irrelevant when a meta flag is present.
5. **Parse errors are deferred:** invalid option values/unknown options do not abort the scan; the first such error is reported (stdout, exit 1) only if no meta flag is encountered.
6. **Validation in this area happens at parse time:** `--output-format` accepts exactly `text`, `sarif`, `xml`, `xmlv2`, `xmlv3` (case-sensitive; `xml` is the deprecated alias and prints NO deprecation warning) — else `cppcheck: error: argument to '--output-format=' must be 'text', 'sarif', 'xml' (deprecated), 'xmlv2' or 'xmlv3'.`. `--xml-version` must parse as an integer (`... is not valid - not an integer.`) and be 2 or 3 (`'--xml-version' can only be 2 or 3.`). `--template`/`--template-location` accept ANY string with no validation.
7. **These options require the `=` form.** Space-separated values make the option itself "unrecognized": `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--template".` (etc.).
8. **Exit codes:** 0 for all meta commands; 1 for parse errors, for "no C or C++ source files found.", and for the std.cfg failure.

| `--output-file=.../out.txt --version` | `Cppcheck 2.19 dev`; out.txt NOT created |
| `--template=gcc --version` | `Cppcheck 2.19 dev` |
| `--output-file=.../out.txt --help` | == `--help`; out.txt NOT created |
| `--xml --help` | == `--help` |
| `--errorlist /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | == `--errorlist` (input files ignored) |

Every command below exits **0** with the meta output on stdout, stderr empty — the parse error is silently discarded:

| Command | Output |
|---|---|
| `--output-format=bad --version` | version |
| `--version --output-format=bad` | version |
| `--output-format=bad --errorlist` | errorlist |
| `--xml-version=9 --errorlist` | errorlist |
| `--std=bad --errorlist` | errorlist |
| `--bogus-flag --errorlist` | errorlist (unknown option BEFORE meta still discarded!) |
| `--errorlist --bogus-flag` | errorlist |
| `--help --bogus-flag` | help |
| `--bogus-flag --help` | help |

Meta vs meta — **the FIRST meta flag on the command line wins**:

| Command | Output |
|---|---|
| `--version --errorlist` | version |
| `--errorlist --version` | errorlist |
| `--help --version` | help |
| `--version --help` | version |
| `--help --errorlist` | help |
| `--errorlist --help` | errorlist |

Consistent model: argument parsing scans left to right; encountering `--help`/`--version`/`--errorlist` prints and exits 0 IMMEDIATELY. Value/unknown-option errors are DEFERRED (collected during the scan, reported only if parsing completes without hitting a meta flag) — which is why `--bogus-flag --errorlist` still prints the errorlist.

## 7. Space-separated option forms are NOT accepted (area options require `=`)

Each of these exits 1, stderr empty, stdout:
| Command | Stdout |
|---|---|
| `--template gcc /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--template".$` |
| `--template-location '{file}' /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--template-location".$` |
| `--output-file X /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--output-file".$` |
| `--output-format text /tmp/probe_output/a.c` | `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--output-format".$` |

2. **`--output-file` never captures anything in this broken-install state.** With analysis it is never even created (failure happens first); with meta commands (`--errorlist`/`--version`/`--help`) it is also ignored — output stays on stdout and the file is not created.

5. **Parse errors are deferred:** invalid option values/unknown options do not abort the scan; the first such error is reported (stdout, exit 1) only if no meta flag is encountered.

7. **These options require the `=` form.** Space-separated values make the option itself "unrecognized": `cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--template".` (etc.).
8. **Exit codes:** 0 for all meta commands; 1 for parse errors, for "no C or C++ source files found.", and for the std.cfg failure.
9. **Repeated options are allowed** (e.g. `--output-format=text --output-format=sarif`) — no error; last value wins.
10. **`-` is not a special file argument** — it is rejected as an unrecognized option.

args.content:
# AREA: file-options (areaname: fileopts) — findings report

Binary: `/workspace/executable.orig` ("Cppcheck 2.19 dev"), run from `/workspace`.
Probe dir: `/tmp/probe_fileopts/` containing `a.c` with content `int main(){return 0;}\n`.
Method: every probe run as `./executable.orig ARGS >/tmp/o 2>/tmp/e </dev/null` (stdin redirected
except where noted); streams captured separately and shown **verbatim** below. `$` at end of a
line in `cat -A` output = newline; there are no trailing spaces anywhere. Unless noted, stderr
was empty and exit code was 1.

## 0. Baseline (the std.cfg failure)

`./executable.orig /tmp/probe_fileopts/a.c`

exit=1, stderr=(empty), stdout (exactly two lines, both newline-terminated):
```
cppcheck: Failed to load library configuration file 'std.cfg'. File not found
Failed to load std.cfg. Your Cppcheck installation is broken, please re-install. The Cppcheck binary was compiled with FILESDIR set to "/usr/local/share/Cppcheck" and will therefore search for std.cfg in /usr/local/share/Cppcheck/cfg.
```

This two-line message is the terminal failure for ANY run that gets past command-line
validation with at least one source file. It always goes to **stdout**, never stderr, and is
never redirected into `--output-file`.

---

## 1. `--project=<file>`

### 1.1 Nonexistent project files (any extension / no extension)

`./executable.orig --project=nosuch.sln /tmp/probe_fileopts/a.c` — exit=1, stderr=(empty):
```
cppcheck: error: failed to open project 'nosuch.sln'. The file does not exist.
```
Identical message (with the given name substituted) for `nosuch.vcxproj`, `nosuch.bpr`,
`nosuch.json`, `nosuch` (no extension), `nosuch.xyz`, and `--project=` (empty value →
`failed to open project ''. The file does not exist.`). Extension plays no role in the
existence check; the same error appears with or without a positional source file.

### 1.2 Existing but malformed project files

`bad.sln` = `garbage\n`:
```
cppcheck: error: Visual Studio solution file header not found
cppcheck: error: failed to load project '/tmp/probe_fileopts/bad.sln'. An error occurred.
```

`bad.vcxproj` = `garbage\n`:
```
cppcheck: error: Visual Studio project file is not a valid XML - XML_ERROR_PARSING_TEXT
cppcheck: error: failed to load project '/tmp/probe_fileopts/bad.vcxproj'. An error occurred.
```

`bad.bpr` = `garbage\n`:
```
cppcheck: error: Borland project file is not a valid XML - XML_ERROR_PARSING_TEXT
cppcheck: error: failed to load project '/tmp/probe_fileopts/bad.bpr'. An error occurred.
```

So: format-specific first line, then the generic
`cppcheck: error: failed to load project '%1%'. An error occurred.` second line. Both stdout, exit=1.

### 1.3 compile_commands.json

`malformed.json` = `not json at all {{{\n`; `obj.json` = `{"foo": 1}` — both give:
```
cppcheck: error: compilation database is not a JSON array
cppcheck: error: failed to load project '/tmp/probe_fileopts/malformed.json'. An error occurred.
```

`nokeys.json` = `[{"directory":"/tmp/probe_fileopts"}]`:
```
cppcheck: error: no 'arguments' or 'command' field found in compilation database entry
cppcheck: error: failed to load project '/tmp/probe_fileopts/nokeys.json'. An error occurred.
```

`nodir.json` = `[{"command":"gcc -c a.c","file":"a.c"}]`:
```
cppcheck: error: 'directory' field in compilation database entry missing
cppcheck: error: failed to load project '/tmp/probe_fileopts/nodir.json'. An error occurred.
```

`nofile.json` = `[{"directory":"/tmp/probe_fileopts","command":"gcc -c a.c"}]` — NOTE: this one
does NOT print the "failed to load project" line; the entry is skipped and loading continues:
```
cppcheck: error: skip compilation database entry because it does not have a proper 'file' field
cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.
```

**CRASH:** `num.json` = `[123]` (array whose element is not an object):
- exit=134 (SIGABRT, "Aborted (core dumped)" from the shell), stdout=(empty), stderr:
```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  "type mismatch! call is<type>() before get<type>()" && is<object>()
```
(the `what():` line starts with exactly two spaces).

`empty.json` = `[]` (also when the file is literally named `compile_commands.json`):
```
cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.
```

`empty.json` **plus positional `a.c`**:
```
cppcheck: error: --project cannot be used in conjunction with source files.
```
(This check happens AFTER the project file is successfully loaded: with a nonexistent
project + positional files you get the "failed to open project" error instead.)

Valid db `valid1.json` = `[{"directory":"/tmp/probe_fileopts","command":"gcc -c a.c","file":"a.c"}]`
(alone, no positional files) → proceeds to the std.cfg two-liner. Same for a db using
`"arguments":["gcc","-c","a.c"]` instead of `"command"`, and same for a db whose `file`
points at a nonexistent `ghost.c` (existence of the compiled file is not checked before
std.cfg load).

---

## 2. `--library=<name>`

`--library=nosuch`, `--library=std`, `--library=posix`, `--library=/path/to/existing/lib.cfg`
(with valid-looking XML), all with `a.c` → all produce the std.cfg two-liner (stdout, exit=1).
The bundled `std` library is always loaded first and fails before any `--library` value is
resolved, so neither missing names nor malformed library files are ever diagnosed.

Exception — `--library=` (empty value):
```
cppcheck: error: empty library specified.
```
exit=1, stderr=(empty). This is validated at parse time.

---

## 3. `--rule` / `--rule-file` — build has NO rules support

Every combination — `--rule='a.*b'`, `--rule='['` (invalid regex), `--rule-file=nosuch`,
`--rule-file=<malformed xml>`, `--rule-file=<valid rule xml>` — gives (stdout, exit=1, stderr empty):
```
cppcheck: error: Option --rule cannot be used as Cppcheck has not been built with rules support.
```
resp.
```
cppcheck: error: Option --rule-file cannot be used as Cppcheck has not been built with rules support.
```
The file is never opened; the regex is never compiled. This is a parse-time rejection
(beats a later `--suppressions-list=nosuch` when `--rule` appears first on the command line).

---

## 4. Suppression file options

### 4.1 `--suppressions-list=<file>`

Nonexistent:
```
cppcheck: error: couldn't open the file: "nosuch".
```
(exit=1, stdout; note the trailing period and double quotes).

Existing file with line `bogus id with spaces:file.c`:
```
cppcheck: error: Failed to add suppression. Invalid id "bogus id with spaces"
```
(error message contains only the id part, before the `:` separator.)

Existing file with lines `bogusline*:::###`, `unusedFunction`, `*:*.h`, comment lines
(`// comment line`), or blank lines → accepted, proceeds to std.cfg two-liner.
Passing a directory as the file also "succeeds" (proceeds to std.cfg failure).

### 4.2 `--exitcode-suppressions=<file>`

Nonexistent → same as suppressions-list:
```
cppcheck: error: couldn't open the file: "nosuch".
```
File containing `bogus suppression` (space in id):
```
cppcheck: error: Failed to add suppression. Invalid id "bogus suppression"
```
File containing `unusedFunction` → std.cfg two-liner.

### 4.3 `--suppress-xml=<file>`

Nonexistent:
```
cppcheck: error: failed to load suppressions XML 'nosuch' (XML_ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND).
```
Malformed `<not xml`:
```
cppcheck: error: failed to load suppressions XML '/tmp/probe_fileopts/bad.xml' (XML_ERROR_PARSING_ATTRIBUTE).
```
Plain text `not xml`:
```
cppcheck: error: failed to load suppressions XML '/tmp/probe_fileopts/bad2.xml' (XML_ERROR_PARSING_TEXT).
```
(i.e. the TinyXML2 error name is interpolated into the parentheses.)

Well-formed but wrong element — `<suppressions><suppression id="x"/></suppressions>`:
```
cppcheck: error: invalid suppression xml file '/tmp/probe_fileopts/s3.xml', expected 'suppress' element but got a 'suppression'.
```

Well-formed `<suppress>` with `id` as an ATTRIBUTE — `<suppressions><suppress id="unmatchedSuppression"/></suppressions>`:
```
cppcheck: error: Failed to add suppression. No id.
```
(Same with an extra `fileName="x.c"` attribute.) The id must be a CHILD element:
`<suppressions><suppress><id>unmatchedSuppression</id></suppress></suppressions>` → accepted,
proceeds to std.cfg two-liner. Empty `<suppressions></suppressions>` also accepted.

---

## 5. `--includes-file` / `--config-excludes-file`

`--includes-file=nosuch`:
```
cppcheck: error: unable to open includes file at 'nosuch'
```
`--config-excludes-file=nosuch`:
```
cppcheck: error: unable to open config excludes file at 'nosuch'
```
(no trailing period on either). Existing files (any content, even a directory path) →
std.cfg two-liner. Contents are never validated before the std.cfg failure.

---

## 6. `--file-list=<file>` / `--file-list=-`

`--file-list=nosuch`:
```
cppcheck: error: couldn't open the file: "nosuch".
```
(same message as `--suppressions-list`.)

- List containing `/tmp/probe_fileopts/a.c` and a nonexistent file → std.cfg two-liner
  (listed files are NOT existence-checked before std.cfg load).
- List containing only a `.txt` file → std.cfg two-liner (no extension filtering at this stage).
- Empty list file, a directory as the list file, or `--file-list=-` with empty stdin →
```
cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.
```
- `--file-list=-` with `/tmp/probe_fileopts/a.c\n` on stdin → std.cfg two-liner (works).
- `--file-list=flist.txt` combined with positional `a.c` → allowed, std.cfg two-liner
  (unlike `--project`, no "conjunction" error).

---

## 7. `--addon=<x>`

`--addon=nosuch`, `--addon=misra`, `--addon=/tmp/x.py` (existing script),
`--addon=<malformed json file>`, `--addon=<valid addon json>` — all with `a.c` → all just
produce the std.cfg two-liner. Addons are not resolved/validated before the std.cfg failure.

---

## 8. `--cppcheck-build-dir=<dir>`

Nonexistent dir (with or without source files):
```
cppcheck: error: Directory '/tmp/probe_fileopts/build' specified by --cppcheck-build-dir argument has to be existent.
```
Same message when the path exists but is a regular file. The directory is NOT created.
With a pre-existing empty directory → std.cfg two-liner, and **no files appear in the
directory** (verified: still empty afterwards). With existing dir but no source files →
`cppcheck: error: no C or C++ source files found.`
So the order is: dir-existence check → source enumeration → std.cfg load.

---

## 9. Output-redirecting options

### 9.1 `--output-file=<file>`
`--output-file=/tmp/probe_fileopts/out.txt a.c` → std.cfg two-liner still printed to
**stdout**; the output file is **never created**. Also not created for parse errors
(`--bogus-flag`) or for `no C or C++ source files found.` — i.e. in this broken-install
environment `--output-file` never produces a file at all, and nothing is ever rerouted.

### 9.2 `--plist-output=<dir>`
Nonexistent dir (or a path that is a regular file):
```
cppcheck: error: plist folder does not exist: '/tmp/probe_fileopts/plist'.
```
(exit=1, stdout; trailing period). Pre-existing empty dir → std.cfg two-liner; the dir
stays empty (no plist files written). Unlike `--cppcheck-build-dir` this check happens at
parse time (see precedence below).

### 9.3 `--checkers-report=<file>`
`--checkers-report=/tmp/probe_fileopts/report.txt a.c` → std.cfg two-liner; **no report file
is written** (also not when the parent dir doesn't exist — the path is never validated or
opened before std.cfg load).
`--checkers-report` WITHOUT `=value`:
```
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--checkers-report".
```
(i.e. the `=` form is mandatory; space-separated value is not accepted.)

---

## 10. `--debug*` flags

Recognized (accepted, then std.cfg two-liner, no extra output whatsoever before failing):
`--debug`, `--debug-normal`, `--debug-simplified`, `--debug-warnings`, `--debug-valueflow`.

NOT recognized:
```
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--debug-templates".
cppcheck: error: unrecognized command line option: "--debug-template-max".
```

---

## 11. Precedence probes (which error wins)

All errors below are stdout/exit=1. Notation: `A > B` = A's error printed.

| Command-line (both options bad) | Winner |
|---|---|
| `--project=nosuch.sln --suppressions-list=nosuch` | project |
| `--suppressions-list=nosuch --project=nosuch.sln` | suppressions-list |
| `--file-list=nosuch --project=nosuch.sln` | file-list |
| `--project=nosuch.sln --file-list=nosuch` | project |
| `--includes-file=nosuch --config-excludes-file=nosuch` | includes |
| `--config-excludes-file=nosuch --includes-file=nosuch` | config-excludes |
| `--includes-file=nosuch --project=nosuch.sln` | includes |
| `--project=nosuch.sln --includes-file=nosuch` | project |
| `--suppress-xml=nosuch --suppressions-list=nosuch` | suppress-xml |
| `--suppressions-list=nosuch --suppress-xml=nosuch` | suppressions-list |
| `--bogus --project=nosuch.sln` | unrecognized option |
| `--project=nosuch.sln --bogus` | project |
